_readme: TEMPLATE ONLY - placeholders, no real assertions. Copy to tests/gold_research.json (which is Git-ignored) after YOUR build, read the actual values from your own database, and replace every <...> placeholder. validate --catalog reads three top-level keys: catalogue_build_id (must equal meta.build_id), cases (assertions; equals uses dotted paths, contains matches anywhere in the JSON text), and optional build_inputs (compared by sha256 only). See docs/RESEARCH.md and docs/VALIDATION.md.
basis: Pinned to the catalogue build_id below. Replace this paragraph with your own provenance note: which inputs, which builder revision, what the pin is meant to detect. These cases are re-derived from the same database, so they detect drift and regression, not ground truth.
catalogue_build_id: <cat_...: copy meta.build_id from your built catalogue>

cases.status: <expected status, e.g. ok; omit to skip the status check>
contains: <substring expected anywhere in the response JSON>

cases._why: search_all_codebooks returns match_quality per hit (token_exact > substring_case_sensitive > substring_case_insensitive) and sorts by it before document kind. Pin one short ASCII token that also occurs inside longer English words, so the assertion fails if ranking regresses to plain kind/path order.

equals.data.results.0.document_id: <document_id of the token-bearing document in YOUR build>
